summary: Chronicle SIEM onboarding: signed delivery receipts, per-tenant sequence guarantees, and sample mapping
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Northbridge Financial) is onboarding Redwood audit feed into Google Chronicle. They require cryptographically signed delivery receipts for each batch, strict per-tenant ordering guarantees with a resume token, and a sample field mapping tailored to Chronicle's schema (including explicit timezone normalization rules). Customer also requests an SFTP fallback for manifest delivery and proof of non-repudiation for legal retention.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete SIEM ingestion and mapping validation.
- Potential delay to security/incident response integrations.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted audit export, production tenant: northbridge-001, expected throughput ~300-800 events/sec during business hours, events include API calls, auth events, and model invocation metadata.

Request:
1) Provide a sample batch (JSONL) with per-record and per-batch headers showing canonicalized timestamp (UTC ISO8601), tenant_id, event_uuid, sequence_number, and optional resume_token.
2) Demonstrate ed25519-signed per-batch manifest and HMAC-SHA256 per-record envelope example.
3) Provide mapping table to Chronicle fields and an example ingestion snippet.
4) Confirm ordering guarantees and behavior under retry/duplicate deliveries.
5) Outline SFTP fallback manifest rotation and verification procedure.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer configured Redwood audit export to deliver to Chronicle pull endpoint.
2) Customer attempted to validate incoming batches; discovered no signature header and inconsistent timezone presentation.
3) Customer attempted partial replays and found out-of-order sequence numbers when retries occurred.
4) Customer opened this ticket requesting signed-manifest and sequence/resume semantics clarity.
logs:
Customer provided sample failed batch (attached in ticket): batch_20260309_14.jsonl (showed local timezone offsets, missing 'signature' header, and duplicate event_uuid entries after retry).
Redwood delivery logs: delivery_id=del-9a7f3b, attempts=3, last_status=200 from Chronicle with no signature-ack.
S3 manifest generator logs: manifest-gen v1.3.2 emitted 'unsigned' flag for the batch due to missing KEK binding for tenant northbridge-001.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Support triage: validated attachments and confirmed missing signature header in delivered batches.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Eng (SRE) checked manifest-generator: found fallback path that emits unsigned manifests when tenant KMS key not bound. Hypothesis: tenant key binding not completed for northbridge-001.
2026-03-10 14:30 - Security reviewed proposed ed25519 signing approach; approved if key rotation and attestation are logged to audit chain.

2026-03-11 08:20 - Determined out-of-order sequence occurs when a failed upload is retried and batch-level sequence_number is regenerated. Need deterministic resume_token per upload attempt to allow Chronicle to dedupe/restore ordering.

2026-03-11 10:05 - Created GH PR to add deterministic resume_token (sha256 of tenant+batch_timestamp+nonce) and switch manifest-gen to sign with tenant-specific ed25519 key when KMS binding present (PR #4982).
2026-03-12 09:00 - Performed internal test delivering signed manifest to Chronicle dev account; Chronicle accepted and returned signature-ack header; ordering preserved when resume_token included.
comments: Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer request attached, asked for immediate sample and mapping. SLA P1 first response due 2026-03-11.
Marco Villanueva (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged, raised to infra and security for sign-off. Asking customer for tenant KMS thumbprint and preferred signature scheme (ed25519 or rsa-pss).
Customer (Northbridge SecOps) 2026-03-10: Prefer ed25519 and need evidence for legal retention (chain-of-custody). Provided KMS thumbprint: kmsthumb-northbridge-42.

SRE (Rina Patel) 2026-03-11: Found missing KMS binding for tenant; manual binding scheduled. Will run end-to-end test once binding is present. Suggested interim workaround: enable S3 manifest HMAC with shared secret to satisfy Chronicle while ed25519 is enabled.
Security (Jon Becker) 2026-03-11: Approved ed25519 with per-batch key rotation policy documented. Require Confluence note and audit log of rotation events.

Marco Villanueva 2026-03-12: Delivered sample payloads and mapping file in ticket attachments (sample_batch.jsonl, chronicle_mapping_v1.csv). Deployed PR #4982 to staging and ran verification against Chronicle dev account. Customer scheduled validation call for 2026-03-15.
Customer 2026-03-12: Received samples and confirmed they match Chronicle dev ingestion script. Asked for SFTP manifest example and a resume_token spec for their compliance team.
resolution:
Provided artifacts: (1) sample JSONL batch with canonical UTC timestamps and per-record sequence_number and event_uuid, (2) chronicle_mapping_v1.csv mapping, (3) signed per-batch manifest using tenant ed25519 key (details and verification steps documented), (4) SFTP fallback manifest spec with rotation and verification commands, and (5) added deterministic resume_token generation (sha256 tenant+batch_ts+nonce) to manifest generator (PR #4982).

Workaround before KMS binding: enabled HMAC-SHA256 per-record envelope using tenant shared secret; Chronicle accepted HMAC verification.

Follow-ups: SUP-880500 created to track automated KMS binding checklist and post-onboarding audit sign-off. Scheduled validation call on 2026-03-15 with customer. Ticket will be closed after successful production validation and confirmation of receipts from Chronicle.
